title: Light Speed Stop 2: Venus Is Hell

summary: Answer: Venus is first when closest (~38 million km, ~2 light-minutes); Mars ~3 min, Sun 8 min 20 s. Venus: ~465°C (melts lead), pressure like 900 m underwater, spins backwards (Sun rises in the west), day longer than its year, Soviet Venera 13 lasted ~2 hours in 1982. Next stop: Mars.

scenes.narration: Venus wins. But only when it lines up perfectly.
At its closest, Venus is thirty eight million kilometres away. Light gets there in about two minutes.
Mars takes at least three. The Sun takes eight minutes and twenty seconds.
So you dive into Venus. Bad idea.
The surface is around four hundred sixty five degrees Celsius. Hot enough to melt lead.
The air is so thick, standing there feels like being nine hundred metres underwater.
And it spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west.
One day on Venus lasts longer than its entire year.
In 1982, a Soviet lander touched down and survived just over two hours.
Then the heat and pressure crushed it.
So you leave. Next stop: the red planet.
Could humans ever live on Mars? Yes or no? Tell me below.
